prs.title: fix: close the gaps the eight-repo compare sweep found
prs.body:
## Why

A sweep of eight public repositories on `a7e479f` found 40 jobs where `wrkflw compare` disagreed with GitHub. They trace to ten causes. One is not wrkflw's: rust-lang/log's doc job fails on Rust 1.100, which came out after the GitHub run. This PR fixes eight of the other nine and leaves one for a follow-up.

## What changes

| Cause | Repos hit | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A composite action's `$GITHUB_PATH` / `$GITHUB_ENV` writes never reached the job (`taiki-e/install-action`, then `cargo hack`: "no such command") | rust-lang/log, 5 jobs | The composite collects what its steps applied and appends it to the calling step's files, on failure too |
| Checkout dropped every symlink | commander.js, 9 jobs | Links are copied as links with the same target, never followed; a changed or removed link follows the repository |
| `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@clippy` / `@miri` were passed to rustup as toolchain names | itoa, 2 jobs | Those branches mean nightly plus `clippy` / `miri, rust-src` unless the step says otherwise. `@master`, `@v1` and every `actions-rs/toolchain` ref pin the action, not a toolchain |
| The job image lacked runner tools (`gh`, `sudo`, `jq`, `unzip`, `python3`, …), and a job with no setup action ran on bare `ubuntu:latest` | itoa, 3 jobs; many more in general | A shared layer adds the tools, plus `gh` from GitHub's apt repository (best effort). Every unmapped job in Docker or Podman now gets this image, and `~/.cargo/bin` is on PATH when Rust is installed |
| A literal `windows-latest` mapped to a servercore image a Linux engine can't start; `macos-*` mapped to `rust:latest` | cobra, log | Both run as Linux in the Ubuntu image, as matrix legs already did. `-P` still maps them to an image of your own |
| Windows jobs run as Linux counted as disagreements | cobra, log | `compare` leaves them out of the agreement count ("not compared: ran as Linux locally…"). macOS jobs are still compared |
| `compare` couldn't pair a called workflow's jobs (`pre_ci` vs `pre_ci / pre_ci`) | itoa | `<caller> / <job>` rows pair with the caller's one result: failed if any failed, skipped if all were |
| A job whose steps run `docker` failed without saying why | cobra | `compare` notes that it needs `WRKFLW_DOCKER_IN_JOBS=1` |
| setup-go refused ranges such as `^1.22` | cobra | `^`, `~` and `>=` resolve to the newest release they allow; a range bounded from above is still refused |

`scripts/conformance/compare_sweep.sh` and `compare_runs.txt` replace the ad-hoc sweep script. The old script counted `✔` lines, which test output also prints (commander.js showed "8898 agree"). The new one reads `compare`'s JSON report and keeps its clones under `~/.cache/wrkflw-sweep`, not `/tmp`.

## Not in this PR

- **Steps still run as root.** GitHub runs them as `runner`, so cobra's `TestFailGenFishCompletionFile`, which expects a permission error, still fails here. Running as another user needs the workspace (a host bind mount on Linux, a volume on macOS) and every toolchain directory (rustup, uv's Pythons, npm's global prefix) to be writable by that user, or every `pip install` and `cargo install` breaks. That's a change of its own, with its own tests. The README now states the gap.
- `compare` doesn't yet warn when a GitHub run is old enough for a floating toolchain to have moved, as with log's doc job. The README says to compare against a recent run.

## Compatibility

- Every job image is rebuilt once: the shared layer changed. The tools-only image is about 1.2 GB and shared by every job.
- Jobs without setup actions now run in a built image instead of bare `ubuntu:latest`. `container:` jobs and images mapped with `-P` are unchanged.
- A Windows image is no longer used for `windows-*` unless mapped with `-P`.
- `wrkflw_executor::script_commands` is now public, so `compare` can tell which jobs run `docker`.

## Testing

- New unit tests: composite env hand-on, symlink checkout (relative, chained, dangling, directory, absolute, changed, removed), rust-toolchain refs, Go ranges, the tools image and its tag, label mapping, called-workflow pairing, the Docker note.
- New container test `a_composite_actions_path_and_env_reach_the_job`, run against Docker.
- Ran a throwaway workflow on Docker: every tool is in the built image (`gh` 2.105), `sudo -n true` works, a symlinked fixture arrives as a link, and a `windows-latest` job runs as Linux.
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo test --workspace` with Docker running: still running when this PR was opened; results to follow in a comment.
- Not run yet: the eight-repo sweep, including the click benchmark (11/11 before). It runs other projects' CI, so it's for the reviewer to run: `scripts/conformance/compare_sweep.sh scripts/conformance/compare_runs.txt target/release/wrkflw`.
